questions.question: Who among the following is considered the pioneer of the Aligarh Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Syed Ahmad Khan.
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan is considered the pioneer of the Aligarh Movement. He founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in 1875 (which later became Aligarh Muslim University) to promote Western education among Muslims.

questions.question: The Wahabi Movement in India was primarily centered in which region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Patna.
The Wahabi Movement in India was primarily centered in Patna (Bihar). It was started by Syed Ahmed Barelvi in the 1820s and aimed at reforming Muslim society and waging jihad against the British.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Permanent Settlement of Bengal was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793.
Reason (R): Under this system, the zamindars were made the owners of the land and were responsible for collecting revenue from the peasants.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
  • Assertion (A) is true: The Permanent Settlement of Bengal was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793.
  • Reason (R) is true: Under this system, zamindars were made the owners of the land and were responsible for collecting revenue from the peasants.
  • R correctly explains A by describing the key feature of the Permanent Settlement.

questions.question: Who was the Governor-General of India when the Indian Penal Code (IPC) was introduced?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Canning.
The Indian Penal Code (IPC) was introduced in 1860 during the tenure of Lord Canning (1856-1862). It was drafted by the first Law Commission chaired by Lord Macaulay.

questions.question: Which of the following was the main objective of the Cripps Mission (1942)?
questions.option_1: To propose Dominion status for India after the war
questions.option_2: To partition India into two nations
questions.option_3: To suppress the Quit India Movement
questions.solution:
The correct answer is To propose Dominion status for India after the war.
The Cripps Mission (1942) was sent by the British government to secure Indian cooperation for World War II. Its main objective was to propose Dominion status for India after the war, along with the right to secede from the Commonwealth. Mahatma Gandhi called it 'a post-dated cheque drawn on a failing bank'.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the 'Indian Home Rule Society' in London in 1905?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Shyamji Krishna Varma.
Shyamji Krishna Varma founded the 'Indian Home Rule Society' in London in 1905. He also established 'India House' and published 'The Indian Sociologist' journal.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25):
1. It was a movement for the right of lower caste people to use the roads surrounding the Vaikom temple.
2. The satyagraha was led by Periyar E.V. Ramasamy and supported by Mahatma Gandhi.
3. The movement was successful in achieving complete temple entry for all castes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.
  • Statement 1 is correct: The Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25) was a movement for the right of lower caste people to use the roads surrounding the Vaikom temple in Travancore (Kerala).
  • Statement 2 is correct: The satyagraha was led by Periyar E.V. Ramasamy and supported by Mahatma Gandhi.
  • Statement 3 is incorrect: The movement achieved the opening of the roads to all castes, but complete temple entry was not achieved at that time.

questions.question: The famous revolutionary song 'Sarfaroshi Ki Tamanna' was written by
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ram Prasad Bismil.
The famous revolutionary song 'Sarfaroshi Ki Tamanna' was written by Ram Prasad Bismil, who was also a freedom fighter involved in the Kakori train robbery (1925).

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Indian to pass the Indian Civil Services (ICS) examination?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Satyendranath Tagore.
Satyendranath Tagore (brother of Rabindranath Tagore) was the first Indian to pass the Indian Civil Services (ICS) examination in 1863.

questions.question: The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly of India was held on:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is December 9, 1946.

The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on December 9, 1946, at the Constitution Hall (now Central Hall of Parliament House) in New Delhi.

  • Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was the interim president (temporary chairman).
  • Dr. Rajendra Prasad was later elected as the permanent President of the Assembly.
  • The Muslim League boycotted the first meeting.

questions.question: Who was the Chairman of the Constituent Assembly of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dr. Rajendra Prasad.

Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the President (Chairman) of the Constituent Assembly on December 11, 1946.

  • He later became the first President of India (1950-1962).
  • The Constituent Assembly had 389 members initially (later reduced to 299 after partition).
  • The Assembly took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to complete the Constitution.

questions.question: The Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution had how many members?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 7.

The Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution was appointed on August 29, 1947.

  • Chairman: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
  • Other members: N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer, K.M. Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadullah, N. Madhava Rau, T.T. Krishnamachari
  • The committee drafted the Constitution and submitted its report on November 26, 1949.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution of India was adopted on November 26, 1949.
2. The Constitution of India came into effect on January 26, 1950.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

  • Statement 1 is correct: The Constitution was adopted on November 26, 1949 (celebrated as Constitution Day or Samvidhan Divas).
  • Statement 2 is correct: It came into effect on January 26, 1950 to commemorate the Purna Swaraj declaration of 1930.

questions.question: The phrase 'We, the people of India' in the Preamble signifies that the source of authority of the Constitution is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is The People of India.

The Preamble begins with 'We, the people of India', which establishes that the Constitution derives its authority from the citizens of India.

  • It emphasizes popular sovereignty.
  • The phrase was borrowed from the US Constitution.
  • It was added to emphasize that the Constitution is a gift of the people to themselves.

questions.question: The word 'Socialist' was added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by which amendment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 42nd Amendment, 1976.

The 42nd Amendment (1976) added three words to the Preamble: Socialist, Secular, and Integrity.

  • It was enacted during the Indira Gandhi government.
  • The original Preamble had only 'Sovereign, Democratic, Republic'.
  • The 42nd Amendment is also known as the 'Mini-Constitution'.

questions.question: Who was the first woman to become the Prime Minister of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Indira Gandhi.

Indira Gandhi became the first woman Prime Minister of India in 1966.

  • She served as Prime Minister from 1966 to 1977 and again from 1980 to 1984.
  • She was the daughter of Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India.
  • She was assassinated in 1984.

questions.question: The 'Tryst with Destiny' speech was delivered by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.

Jawaharlal Nehru delivered the historic 'Tryst with Destiny' speech on the eve of India's independence, August 14, 1947, at the Central Hall of Parliament.

  • The speech marked India's freedom from British rule.
  • It is considered one of the greatest speeches of the 20th century.
  • Nehru became the first Prime Minister of independent India.

questions.question: Who was the first Deputy Prime Minister of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel served as the first Deputy Prime Minister of India from 1947 until his death in 1950.

  • He was also the first Home Minister of India.
  • He is known as the 'Iron Man of India' for integrating princely states.
  • He was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1991.

questions.question: The Constitution of India was handwritten in which two languages?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Hindi and English.

The original Constitution of India was handwritten by Prem Behari Narain Raizada in calligraphy.

  • It was written in both Hindi and English.
  • Each page was decorated by artists from Santiniketan.
  • The original copies are kept in helium-filled cases in the Parliament Library.

questions.question: The minimum age required to become the President of India is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 35 years.

Article 58 of the Indian Constitution prescribes the qualifications for the President of India.

  • Minimum age: 35 years
  • Must be a citizen of India
  • Must be qualified to be a member of the Lok Sabha
  • Must not hold any office of profit under the government

questions.question: Who was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sukumar Sen.

Sukumar Sen served as the first Chief Election Commissioner of India from 1950 to 1958.

  • He conducted the first general elections of India in 1951-52.
  • The Election Commission of India was established on January 25, 1950 (National Voters' Day).
  • He was an Indian civil servant and mathematician.

questions.question: The first general elections in independent India were held in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1951-52.

The first general elections of independent India were held from October 1951 to February 1952.

  • The Indian National Congress (INC) won a landslide victory.
  • Jawaharlal Nehru became the first elected Prime Minister.
  • Voters were given a separate ballot box for each candidate.

questions.question: The number of schedules in the Indian Constitution is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 12.

The Indian Constitution originally had 8 schedules. Currently, it has 12 schedules.

  • The 1st schedule lists states and union territories.
  • The 7th schedule contains the three lists (Union, State, Concurrent).
  • Schedules 9 to 12 were added by subsequent amendments.

questions.question: Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution deals with:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Fundamental Duties.

Part IV-A (Article 51A) was added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976 on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

  • There are 11 Fundamental Duties.
  • They are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts).
  • The 11th duty was added by the 86th Amendment, 2002 (right to education for children aged 6-14).

questions.question: The concept of 'Judicial Review' in India is borrowed from the Constitution of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is United States of America.

Judicial Review is the power of the Supreme Court and High Courts to examine the constitutionality of laws.

  • It was borrowed from the US Constitution.
  • It is implicit in Articles 13, 32, and 226 of the Indian Constitution.
  • India follows a 'procedure established by law' (unlike the US 'due process of law').
